decisions.reason: The existing kernel lemma proves the locally integrable bound |G(x,y)| <= C|x-y|^(1-d), both Schur bounds, compact support and the distributional divergence formula. Thus existence was supplied locally, contrary to the rejection, but justified_by omitted the required registration. Added that lemma to justified_by; the Definition and its claims are unchanged.

Given explicitly defines the vector space as the H1 closure of compactly supported smooth vector fields. Equivalently take the finite Cartesian product of the scalar closure: choose each component within 1/(n sqrt(d)) and assemble, so the squared product norm tends to zero. The finite derivative sum converges in L2 and Holder passes its integral. No vector-valued extension theorem or extra axiom is needed, including for empty D.

F2 cited only a theorem for linear maps, which does not supply translation invariance for x=tz+(1-t)y. Added the existing translation-invariance theorem as a dependency and derived the affine integral substitution from the two measure identities, through indicator/simple functions. Also specified a harmless zero representative on the null diagonal. Verified compact segment support, the annular L1 bounds in both variables, the Schur estimate, and the divergence sign delta_y-omega. Statement unchanged.

The affine substitutions in F2 lacked the translation-invariance dependency; supplied it and derived the integral identity by composing translation and dilation. Also repaired step 3.1: for signed omega, |G| need not dominate truncated kernels, whereas C|x-y|^(1-d) does and is integrable against |f(y)| in both variables. Dominated convergence now gives L1 convergence of the fields. The uniform bound pi|xi_j| ||phi||_1 ||f||_1 justifies the Fourier limit against Schwartz tests. The derivative decomposition retains its minus sign; Statement unchanged.

The published matching affine simplicial mesh convention defines a mesh as a finite set of nondegenerate cells exactly tiling a bounded polyhedral open set. F1 invokes the MINI spaces with their bounded-domain hypotheses and Given explicitly says finite. Thus an infinite mesh is outside this interface. Checked nodal unisolvence, both directions of zero boundary nodal values via closure/trace, independent cell bubbles, and the nonzero mean functional on constants. These give the stated dimensions without an additional finiteness hypothesis.

The claim explicitly defines a local bilinear pairing and assumes the positive interior barycentric bubble; it claims no membership in global MINI or Stokes spaces outside dimensions two and three. For any nondegenerate simplex, applying Gauss-Green to q b_K grad(q), with the product rule, gives the displayed identity because b_K vanishes on the boundary. The affine nonconstant gradient is nonzero, so positivity is strict. In dimension one the same identity is ordinary integration by parts on an interval. Dimension restrictions of the contextual MINI definitions are therefore irrelevant to this local calculation.

F1 states interpolation constants with possible fixed-domain dependence, so merely invoking it did not establish the stronger constant in the theorem. Kept the full claim and added a local derivation: solid-angle bounds limit vertex-star size, qualitative Lipschitz connectivity supplies bounded facet chains, and cell trace/Poincare plus scaled facet dual moments yield local H1 stability and L2 approximation with constants depending only on d and shape regularity. Bounded patch overlap and bubble scaling then give that same dependence for C_F. Domain charts supply connectivity only. Cell-mean preservation and weak integration by parts retain the exact pressure pairing and the inf-sup transfer.
